exposure: Uterine artery (UA) transection during abdominal radical trachelectomy (ART) or abdominal modified radical trachelectomy (AmRT)
cohort: Pregnant women who had undergone abdominal radical trachelectomy (ART) or abdominal modified radical trachelectomy (AmRT) for cervical cancer at Kyushu University Hospital between January 2008 and July 2024.
finding: Uterine artery transection during ART/AmRT increases the risk of abnormal placentation and bleeding-related complications during cesarean section, but it does not increase the risk of other major obstetric complications such as antepartum bleeding or premature birth.
mod_finding: Pregnancies with abnormal placentation after UA transection had significantly more blood loss and required blood transfusions more frequently during cesarean sections.
